TOOLING BURST T4e — SPEC § 7 row "T4e — peak decomposition" (Run C-5, E0-p step 2: the painted fire peak becomes pieces the runtime can fly). task_id "T4e".

Read ONLY, in this order:
1. /Users/admin/Games/reincarnated-collaboration/astra_test_01/burst/SPEC.md — § 0, § 1, and § 7 (the intro paragraph, the row "T4e — peak decomposition" — your contract; its Acceptance column is how your work is measured — and the row "T4h — piece-burst template" that CONSUMES your output; design pieces.json so T4h can read it without guessing).
2. /Users/admin/Games/reincarnated-collaboration/astra_test_01/burst/BURST_RULES.md (the TOOLING row).
3. export/vfx_material.gdshader (the value-index contract: source R carries band = round(R/255×3) ∈ {0,1,2,3}; alpha is independent coverage), export/effect_kit.py (kit schema; `distance_fields`), oracle/vfx_measure.py (coverage conventions), and the INPUT peak: runs/C-5/artifacts/E0p-peak-01/fire_peak_01_512.png — the WORKING asset (the painter delivered 1254²; the conductor resampled it to 512² with Lanczos ×0.408 so the body spans ≈ 306 px = 2.35 BH at 1:1; the raw original fire_peak_01.png is beside it for reference only) (painted by Astra as a four-plane greyscale body on either a transparent background or a flat #00ff00 plate — inspect it first and report which; the receipt runs/C-5/artifacts/E0p-peak-01/receipt.json says what the painter claimed).
Do not read anything else. No web. No agents. No image generation. No pip install. stdlib + Pillow + numpy + scipy ONLY.

BUILD exactly the SPEC row — `oracle/peak_pieces.py` with a CLI (`python3 -m oracle.peak_pieces <peak.png> --out <dir> [--centre x y] [--plate green|alpha|auto]`) and functions: isolate(peak_png, plate='auto') → straight-alpha RGBA body (alpha from the PNG when it has real transparency; otherwise deterministic keying of the flat plate with a ≤ 1-px fringe clamp — report which path ran and the fringe width); quantise(rgba) → value-index map with exactly four bands by nearest of {0, 85, 170, 255} on luminance plus the unchanged alpha, and a `band_histogram`; decompose(index_map, alpha, centre=None) → pieces: connected components split along painted-plane boundaries (watershed / band-boundary split so that no piece spans two bands by more than 5 % of its area; merge slivers < 24 px into their largest band-matching neighbour); per piece: mask PNG (RGBA, index colour + alpha, same canvas, cropped bbox recorded), pivot = the piece's own coverage centroid (must lie inside its mask — if not, use the mask pixel nearest the centroid), radial angle (deg, screen coordinates, 0 = +x, clockwise positive) and distance (px) from the burst centre (= coverage centroid of the whole body unless --centre is given), band index, area px, bbox; write pieces.json {source sha256, canvas, centre, plate_path_used, band_histogram, pieces:[...]} and a contact sheet (pieces tinted per band on the source silhouette, numbered) to the out dir; also write the quantised index PNG (`peak_index.png`, the asset the runtime uses — RGB = band × 85, alpha = coverage).
Tests (unittest, stdlib): a synthetic four-band body with known plane layout → the expected piece count and a union equal to the source coverage; a pivot-outside-mask case (a crescent) resolved to the nearest mask pixel; a two-band-spanning blob split into two pieces; the keyed-plate path on a synthetic green-plate body with ≤ 1-px fringe.
ACCEPTANCE on the real peak (report exact numbers in runs/C-5/t3/T4e/acceptance.json): ≥ 6 and ≤ 40 pieces; union of piece masks == source coverage within ± 0.5 % of area; every pivot inside its own mask; no piece spans two bands by > 5 % of its area; RED: union ≠ source; a pivot outside its mask. If the painter's output is NOT four clean planes (gradients, glow, > 4 levels), do not fix it by heavier quantisation — quantise as specified, report the band histogram and the fraction of pixels farther than 20 luminance levels from their nearest band, and mark the run DELIVERED_WITH_CONCERNS naming the defect (the conductor decides whether the peak is re-painted).
Then run the FULL suite: `cd /Users/admin/Games/reincarnated-collaboration/astra_test_01/burst && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -B tests/run_t0c.py` — expected: all green except the five standing reds (test_f04_outside_at_least_three; three test_named_genuine_annuli_retained subtests; test_synthetic_contract_and_grid); report tests_run, successful, and name every red.

DO NOT touch: lane/, bible/, fixtures/, briefs/, SPEC.md, BURST_RULES.md, REGISTER_CARD.md, JUDGE_RUBRIC.md, MANIFEST.sha256, receipt.schema.json, transcribe.schema.json, export/ (T4h owns the runtime side), any existing test file, anything under runs/ except runs/C-5/t3/T4e/ (write the pieces there: runs/C-5/t3/T4e/pieces/). Do not run git. Temporary files ONLY under runs/C-5/t3/T4e/. Write out/files.json listing every file you added or changed with sha256.
RETURN: the receipt (task_id "T4e"): files = every added/changed path with sha256; images = 0 (INTEGER); calls_used; status DELIVERED / DELIVERED_WITH_CONCERNS / FAILED with concerns listed honestly.
